A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same UCoT research despite the changed title and framing. All 20 pages of v1 and 21 pages of v2, including Appendices A–C, support comparison of the text, equations, figures, and tables.

before.justification: v1 reports original benchmark experiments, component ablations, sensitivity and robustness analyses, and qualitative case studies in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and reports a revised pilot study and additional LightThinker comparison results.

M1.justification: The compressor, placeholder hidden states, two-layer projector, semantic loss, reward factor, and two-stage training procedure are retained. Renaming upfront thoughts as contextual CoT or soft tokens and explicitly describing single-pass generation clarify the existing procedure; Appendix A.6 confirms the algorithmic continuity.

E1.justification: Both versions use GSM8K, MATH-500, AIME 2024, ASDiv, GPQA, and HumanEval. The revised pilot reuses existing datasets and the external-CoT input scenario; its model configuration changes do not establish new task or domain coverage.

E2.justification: LightThinker is added to the latent-reasoning comparison in v2 Table 5, corresponding to v1 Table 13. Depth-Recurrent and Coconut remain, as do Prompt, Truncation, CoD, and Tokenskip in their existing comparisons.

E3.justification: v1 Figure 1 fixes the context generator at Qwen2.5-1.5B and varies executor size on GSM8K. v2 Section 3.2 instead fixes the executor at 7B, varies context generators across 1.5B–14B, and measures contextual and output tokens on GSM8K and MATH-500. The established benchmark splits, training budgets, and decoding settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: The revised pilot examines context-source size and the generation cost behind output-token savings. Decoded-CoT case evidence is reduced from four pairs in v1 Figures 4–5 to two revised pairs in v2 Figures 5–6. The component ablations, information-volume analysis, length sensitivity, model-scale analyses, and prompt-robustness tests are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions retain five-seed averaging in Appendices A.3–A.4. No changed repeated-run counts, uncertainty-reporting practices, confidence intervals, or significance-testing procedures are documented.

E6.justification: v2 replaces the pilot results, adds four LightThinker scores, and revises the decoded-CoT examples; Tables 1–4 remain numerically unchanged. In v1 Table 12 versus v2 Table 13, DeepSeek's AIME token counts change from 12861.6 to 1286.16 for Original, 12089.9 to 1208.24 for Tokenskip at 0.9, and 10933.4 to 1093.34 for UCoT at 0.9. These changes conflict with retained lower-ratio rows and compression ratios.

T1.justification: v2 Section 3.1 explicitly formalizes post-reasoning conditioned on external CoT and compares total output lengths. The vanilla-reasoning formulation replaces the stepwise exposition in v1 Appendix B. The training losses and compression objective remain mathematically equivalent; no new theorem or proof is introduced.

C1.justification: v2 elevates post-reasoning to a separately claimed novel reasoning paradigm and presents UCoT as its efficient realization. v1 centers its contributions on upfront-thought generation, utilization, and performance. This substantially broadens the claimed conceptual contribution, while retaining the headline GSM8K compression and Tokenskip comparison claims.

C2.justification: v2 explicitly explains that shorter executor outputs shift computation to contextual-CoT generation and makes context-generation cost and quality conditions for effective post-reasoning. The structural-guidance interpretation from v1 Appendix C.6 is retained and expanded in the main text. The three stated limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: v2 explicitly identifies the Qwen3-8B backbone in the latent-comparison caption and describes latency as end-to-end, without establishing that timing procedures changed. It removes v1's statement that code and data are in supplementary material. Most hyperparameters, prompts, hardware details, and pseudocode remain available and unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 shifts positioning toward input-side post-reasoning and removes the Small Model Empowerment subsection, including v1's acknowledgment of Liu et al. (2025), Thought Manipulation, as prior external-thought work. It adds relevant references such as SemCoT and gist tokens. Together with the broader novelty claim, this substantially revises the relationship to prior research.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction, method explanation, and conclusion are extensively rewritten around post-reasoning and contextual CoT. A Preliminary section is introduced, and the latent-method comparison and decoded-CoT discussion move from the appendix into Sections 5.6–5.7. This is substantial narrative restructuring.

P2.justification: v2 adds a reasoning-paradigm schematic, replaces the original accuracy–token plot with a dual-axis pilot figure separating contextual and output tokens, updates the workflow diagram, and redesigns the decoded-CoT case figures with highlighted structures. The expanded latent-comparison table moves into the main text, producing substantial changes to key displays and their placement.

improvement.justification: The revised pilot, clearer method explanation, and LightThinker comparison improve motivation and comparative evidence. However, v2 introduces internally inconsistent AIME token counts, removes the code/data availability statement, and advances broader novelty claims while dropping v1's explicit acknowledgment of closely related external-thought work. These material gains and losses prevent a confident judgment of the net change in overall quality.
